name: The Mosaic Company
blurb: The Mosaic Company is one of the world's largest producers and marketers of concentrated phosphate and potash crop nutrients, serving the global agricultural inputs market. It operates through three segments—Phosphates, Potash, and Mosaic Fertilizantes—and owns mines and production facilities that produce diammonium phosphate (DAP), monoammonium phosphate (MAP), MicroEssentials (a value-added ammoniated phosphate), and phosphate-based animal feed ingredients. With approximately 13,249 employees and trailing twelve-month revenue of roughly $12.4 billion, Mosaic is a foundational supplier to the global fertilizer industry. The company went public in October 2004 and is classified in the Materials sector under Agricultural Inputs.
recent: Mosaic reported Q1 2026 results on May 11, 2026, posting a net loss and operating loss with adjusted EBITDA declining year-over-year; net income fell approximately 88% on a trailing basis to $45 million. The company withdrew its phosphate segment guidance due to raw material constraints and announced production curtailments with significant charges in Brazil, while the Potash segment was a relative bright spot with increased sales volumes and earnings. For Q2, management guided DAP prices of $760–$780 per tonne and potash sales volumes of 1.9 million tonnes, and trimmed full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $1.25 billion; the stock, which traded near its 52-week low, closed at $22.78 on May 13, 2026 (+1.74%), well below analyst consensus target of $30.13.
